Premise:
• x and n are integers such that $\gcd(x,n)=1$ [tc_1].

natural_language: If~$R$ is a complete set of residues modulo~$n$ and $a\in\Z$ with $\gcd(a,n)=1$, then $aR = \{ax : x \in R\}$ is also a complete set of residues modulo~$n$.
statement:
Definition:
• It is assumed that if R is a complete set of residues modulo n and a is an integer with $\gcd(a,n)=1$, then the set $aR = \{ax : x \in R\}$ is also a complete set of residues modulo n [def_1].

natural_language:
Let
$$
  P = \{ a : 1\leq a \leq n \text{ and } \gcd(a,n) = 1\}.
$$
statement:
Definition:
• Let P be the set of integers $P = \{ a : 1\leq a \leq n \text{ and } \gcd(a,n) = 1\}$ [def_2].

natural_language: In the same way that we proved Lemma~\ref{lem:residues}, we see that the reductions modulo~$n$ of the elements of $xP$ are the same as the reductions of the elements of $P$.
statement:
We assume:
• x and n are integers such that $\gcd(x,n)=1$ [tc_1].
• The principle that multiplying a complete residue system by a coprime integer permutes the system [def_1].
• P is the set of integers $P = \{ a : 1\leq a \leq n \text{ and } \gcd(a,n) = 1\}$ [def_2].
Therefore, we conclude:
• The set of residues of the elements of $xP$ modulo n is the same as the set of residues of the elements of P modulo n [l1].
lean_hint: Apply the principle from def_1, adapted for a reduced residue system (P), showing that multiplication by x permutes the residues.

natural_language:
Thus
$$
 \prod_{a\in P} (xa) \con \prod_{a \in P} a \pmod{n},
$$
since the products are over the same numbers modulo~$n$.
statement:
We assume:
• P is the set of integers $P = \{ a : 1\leq a \leq n \text{ and } \gcd(a,n) = 1\}$ [def_2].
• The set of residues of the elements of $xP$ modulo n is the same as the set of residues of the elements of P modulo n [l1].
Therefore, we conclude:
• $\prod_{a\in P} (xa) \equiv \prod_{a \in P} a \pmod{n}$ [l2].
lean_hint: If two finite sets of integers are the same modulo n, their products are congruent modulo n. Apply this to the sets of residues from l1.

natural_language: Now cancel the $a$'s on both sides
statement:
We assume:
• P is the set of integers $P = \{ a : 1\leq a \leq n \text{ and } \gcd(a,n) = 1\}$ [def_2].
Therefore, we conclude:
• The product of the elements in P, $\prod_{a \in P} a$, is coprime to n, i.e., $\gcd(\prod_{a \in P} a, n) = 1$ [l3].
lean_hint: The product of integers coprime to n is also coprime to n. Use induction on the set P, where each element is coprime to n by definition.

natural_language:
Now cancel the $a$'s on both sides to get
$$x^{\#P} \con 1\pmod{n},$$
statement:
We assume:
• P is the set of integers $P = \{ a : 1\leq a \leq n \text{ and } \gcd(a,n) = 1\}$ [def_2].
• $\prod_{a\in P} (xa) \equiv \prod_{a \in P} a \pmod{n}$ [l2].
• $\gcd(\prod_{a \in P} a, n) = 1$ [l3].
Therefore, we conclude:
• $x^{\#P} \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$ [l4].
lean_hint: Rewrite the left side of l2 as $x^{\#P} \cdot \prod_{a \in P} a$. Then, use the property l3 to cancel the term $\prod_{a \in P} a$ from both sides of the congruence.

natural_language: The set of units in $\zmod{n}$ is a group... that has order~$\phi(n)$.
statement:
We assume:
• P is the set of integers $P = \{ a : 1\leq a \leq n \text{ and } \gcd(a,n) = 1\}$ [def_2].
• By definition, Euler's totient function $\phi(n)$ counts the number of positive integers up to n that are relatively prime to n.
Therefore, we conclude:
• The cardinality of P is equal to Euler's totient function of n, i.e., $\#P = \phi(n)$ [l5].
lean_hint: Show that the definition of the set P corresponds directly to the definition of Euler's totient function.
Substitute the equality from l5 into the congruence from l4.
